title: An optimized protocol for propidium monoazide treatment
protocol: Thaw PMA dye.
Turn the ThermomMixer to the required temperature.
Put 1 mL sample into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Prepare dead cell controls if sample volume permits.
Heat inactivate the sample at 95°C for 7 min on an Eppendorf ThermoMixer shaking at 400 rpm.
Cool the sample to room temperature.
Confirm killing of microbes using a plating method.
Add 1.25 µL PMA (20mM) to tube caps to obtain a final concentration of 25 µM in dim light.
Gently close the tube and put it into a freezer box immediately, covering the box.
Invert all tubes (the freezer box) simultaneously 5 times.
Vortex the freezer box for 5 seconds.
Wrap the box with aluminum foil.
Band it onto the ThermoMixer.
Shake at 300 rpm.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Quickly transfer the tubes into the PMA-Lite™ device.
Expose samples to light for 15 min.
Every 2 minutes, turn off the device.
Take 3 tubes and vortex together for 2 s.
Turn on the PMA-Lite™ device immediately after vortexing.
Centrifuge the samples at 5,000 x g for 13 minutes.
Pipette out the supernatant into PMA liquid waste.
Add the same volume of buffer as pipetted out.
Resuspend the pellet by brief, vigorous vortexing.
Wrap the tubes with foil.
Put the wrapped tubes in the freezer.
Store the tubes at -20°C or -80°C until DNA extraction.
Measure OD600 of the sample to assess turbidity if sample volume permits.
Make dead cell controls if sample volume permits.
Use DNase-free water to dissolve PMA.
Store reconstituted PMA at -20°C (stable for at least 6 months).
